turn.text:
Send traffic destined to Carrier A via WAN1 and Carrier B via WAN2. If a line goes down, automatically switch to the surviving line, and switch back when it recovers.

Site notes: fw reaches Carrier A (prefix 198.51.100.0/24) through WAN1 on eth2 (next hop 203.0.113.1) and Carrier B (prefix 198.51.200.0/24) through WAN2 on eth3 (next hop 203.0.114.1). Use policy routing (`ip rule` + per-ISP tables) so A-bound traffic exits WAN1 and B-bound exits WAN2, and add a health check (ping the next hop) that moves traffic to the surviving link when one goes down. masquerade is already configured on both uplinks.
Plan: ip route replace 198.51.100.0/24 via 203.0.113.1 dev eth2; ip route replace 198.51.200.0/24 via 203.0.114.1 dev eth3; mkdir -p /etc/nb; cat > /etc/nb/failover.sh <<'EOS'; chmod +x /etc/nb/failover.sh; setsid /etc/nb/failover.sh >/var/log/failover.log 2>&1 &

input.command: true # AGENT-ACTION[C02]: ip route replace 198.51.100.0/24 via 203.0.113.1 dev eth2; ip route replace 198.51.200.0/24 via 203.0.114.1 dev eth3; mkdir -p /etc/nb; cat > /etc/nb/failover.sh <<'EOS' #!/bin/bash while true; do if ping -c1 -W1 203.0.113.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then GW_A=203.0.113.1; DEV_A=eth2; else GW_A=203.0.114.1; DEV_A=eth3; fi if ping -c1 -W1 203.0.114.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then GW_B=203.0.114.1; DEV_B=eth3; else GW_B=203.0.113.1; DEV_B=eth2; fi ip route replace 198.51.100.0/24 via $GW_A dev $DEV_A; ip route replace 198.51.200.0/24 via $GW_B dev $DEV_B sleep 3 done EOS
